result.rationale: Verifiable in the diff: refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, whose own comment states 'The response should only contain the access token and expiry date'. Yet lark's CalendarService passes that response to handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp> (expecting Lark's code/msg/data envelope), zoho's adapters access tokenInfo.data.error (a fetch Response has no .data property), and hubspot treats the Response as HubspotToken. When credential sharing is enabled, these provider-specific parses fail on the sync endpoint's minimal response, breaking token ref

adjudication.rationale: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, `refreshOAuthTokens` stops calling the provider refresh flow and instead POSTs to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and returns that response. However several adapters still process the returned value as if it were the provider-specific refresh response, not the minimal “access token + expiry” contract: (1) `apps-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` passes the returned `resp` into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`, which expects Lark’s refresh JSON shape; (2) `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts` read `tokenInfo.data` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` as if it were an Axios response, but under sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response`, so `.data` will be undefined and the provider-shape checks can’t work; (3) `packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts` now wraps the Microsoft token refresh call with `refreshOAuthTokens` but still treats the result as the Microsoft token endpoint response via `handleErrorsJson<ITokenResponse>(response)` (no `parseRefreshTokenResponse` fallback like office365calendar/zoom/google), so a sync endpoint returning only token+expiry can break expectations. This is a behavioral correctness issue introduced by routing these code paths through the sync endpoint without adapting their parsing/response handling.
